content.title: Most Oscars won by a movie: What films are the biggest winners in Academy Awards history?
content.text: The Academy Awards, commonly known as the Oscars, are one of the most prestigious recognitions in the film industry. Over the years, some productions have stood out not only for their impact on audiences and critics but also for the number of golden statuettes they have won in a single edition. This article explores the movies that have made history by becoming the most awarded at the Oscars.To watch this video, agree to share video information with third partiesAgree|More infoTopping the list is "The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King" (2003), with an unprecedented 11 wins, sweeping categories from Best Picture to Visual Effects, cementing its place in cinematic lore. Alongside it stands "Titanic" (1997), a tale of love and loss amid the tragic sinking of the titular ship, also boasting 11 Oscars under its belt."Ben-Hur" (1959) marches in stride with its 11 Academy Awards, recounting the epic saga of a betrayed prince seeking vengeance in ancient Rome. Meanwhile, "West Side Story" (1961) pirouettes into the spotlight with 10 wins, offering a modern retelling of Shakespearean romance against the backdrop of New York City's gritty streets.Other luminaries grace this illustrious list, from the sweeping romance of "The English Patient" (1996) to the regal retelling of "The Last Emperor" (1987). Musicals like "Gigi" (1958) and "My Fair Lady" (1964) sing their way to victory, while historical epics like "Gandhi" (1982) and "Lawrence of Arabia" (1962) command attention with their grand narratives.Movies with the most Oscar wins1.
